content.text: This section sets out how schools build and keep external partnerships. These partnerships give students more learning opportunities and prepare them for success after secondary school. Eduversal Partner Schools are committed to creating meaningful pathways. These pathways connect students with universities, employers, cultural institutions and alumni networks, so graduates are well prepared for their chosen futures. The external partnerships and student pathways program supports the Schoolwide Learner Outcomes (SLOs), especially Academic Excellence, Global Competence, Communication and Innovation. It also aligns with CIS Domain H (Community and home partnerships) and WASC Category C (Support for Student Personal and Academic Growth).
The following principles guide all external partnerships and pathway programs:
content.title: 23.1.1 Guiding Principles

items: Student-Centered: All partnerships put student benefit, learning outcomes and future opportunities first
Ethical Engagement: Partnerships are transparent, avoid conflicts of interest and uphold school values
Equity and Access: All students, whatever their background or financial situation, can get pathway support
EAL-Inclusive: Programs meet the needs of students whose first language is not English and give them suitable support and resources
Data-Informed: Decisions use data on student outcomes, destination tracking and how well partnerships work
Sustainable: Partnerships are built for long-term benefit to both sides, not for short-term gains

content.text: External partnerships encompass:
content.title: 23.1.2 Scope of External Partnerships

items: Higher Education Institutions: Indonesian and international universities, polytechnics, and vocational institutions
Industry and Business: Companies offering internships, work experience, and career insights
Professional Organizations: Bodies that offer certifications, competitions and professional development
Cultural Institutions: Museums, galleries, libraries and cultural centers that support educational programs
NGOs and Community Organizations: Partners that support service learning, community engagement and social impact
Alumni Network: Graduates who contribute through mentorship, career guidance and support for the school

content.text: The university counseling program gives full support to students as they prepare for higher education. It helps them work through Indonesian and international university admissions processes successfully.
Cross-Reference: Section 1.8 (Organizational Chart - the School College Counselor position), Career Growth Framework 26-27 and Career Growth Role Register 26-27
content.title: 23.2.1 Program Structure and Roles

content.text: Director of College Counseling (Eduversal Level)

items: Develops network-wide university counseling strategies
Works with College Counselors across partner schools
Builds partnerships with universities and admissions organizations
Monitors network-wide university placement outcomes
Organizes cross-school workshops and university fairs

content.text: College Counselor (School Level)

items: Guides individual students through the university application process
Holds one-on-one counseling sessions with students and parents
Organizes school-level workshops, university visits, and information sessions
Tracks application progress and outcomes for the school's students
Works with class teachers on academic preparation and documents
Keeps relationships with university admissions representatives

content.text: Secondary School Principal

items: Oversees how university counseling links with academic programs
Supports the College Counselor with allocating resources and scheduling
Reviews university placement outcomes as part of the school's quality measures

content.title: 23.2.2 Counseling Program Timeline

content.text: Schools give full support for the main university application systems:

content.title: UCAS (Universities and Colleges Admissions Service - UK)

items: Help with writing the personal statement, with 4,000-character guidance
Reference writing following UCAS conventions
Predicted grade preparation and submission
Interview preparation for Oxbridge and competitive courses

Deadline management: use the current-cycle UCAS deadlines, re-checked each year against UCAS and the Quality Ecosystem: External Exams & Admissions 26-27 reference. Never carry them forward from a previous year.
content.title: 23.2.3 Application Platform Support

content.text: Common Application (USA)

items: Essay writing support for the main essay and supplements
Activities list development and description
Counselor recommendation and school profile
Financial aid application guidance (CSS Profile, FAFSA basics)
Early Decision/Early Action strategy

content.text: Indonesian National Systems

items: SNBP (Seleksi Nasional Berdasarkan Prestasi, the national merit-based admission route): Academic ranking and portfolio preparation
SNBT (Seleksi Nasional Berdasarkan Tes, the national test-based admission route): Support with test registration and preparation
Mandiri (Independent Selection): University-specific application guidance
Raport (school report)/transcript preparation that meets Indonesian requirements

content.text: Other Systems

items: Direct university applications (Australia, Singapore, Europe)
Portfolio development for art, design, and architecture programs
Audition preparation for performing arts programs

content.text: Eduversal Partner Schools have a large EAL population (40-70%), so the counseling program includes specific provisions:

Essay support that takes account of language development stages
University recommendations that consider the student's EAL context and progress
Information about foundation/pathway programs for students who need extra preparation
Bilingual parent communication (English and Bahasa Indonesia)
Connections with universities offering strong EAL support services

content.title: Safeguarding due diligence for mentors, hosts, and external instructors
items: Background check: this applies to every alumni mentor, work-experience supervisor and external instructor who will have contact with students. Before any contact begins, each one provides a current SKCK (police clearance) and two checkable references. Checks are renewed annually.
Written agreement: each external adult signs the school safeguarding agreement and completes a safeguarding briefing before their first session.
No unsupervised one-to-one contact, in person or in a private digital channel. Mentoring takes place in a school-monitored setting or on a school-monitored channel.

Monitored communication: all mentor-student communication uses a school-approved channel. Logs are kept for the length of the placement plus one year. Personal phone numbers, personal email and personal social media are not used.
DSL sign-off: the Designated Safeguarding Lead approves every external placement and every mentor match before it starts, and keeps the register.
Concerns: any concern about an external adult is reported to the DSL immediately. It is handled under Section 9, including the allegations-against-adults procedure.

Work experience: placements also confirm the host employer's insurance cover and a named supervisor at the host site. They also confirm the student's working hours against Indonesian child-labor limits.

content.text: Ethical screening: the school does not promote scholarship sponsors whose core business conflicts with the safeguarding and wellbeing duties in Sections 9 and 22. Tobacco, alcohol, gambling and vaping sponsors are excluded. Government programs and university awards have no such restriction.

content.title: 23.7.1 Partnership Approval Process
content.text: All formal external partnerships require the correct level of approval. See the partnership approval levels table below.

content.title: 23.7.2 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) Template
content.text: Formal partnerships are recorded in MOUs (Memoranda of Understanding) that contain: Essential MOU Elements:

steps: Parties: Full legal names of the school (Yayasan) and the partner organization
Purpose: A clear statement of the partnership's goals
Scope: Specific activities and programs covered
Duration: Start date, end date, renewal terms
Responsibilities: The detailed duties of each party
Resources: Financial contributions, in-kind support, staffing
Intellectual Property: Who owns the materials created
Confidentiality: Data sharing and privacy requirements
Safeguarding: Child protection commitments
Liability: Insurance requirements, indemnification
Termination: Conditions for ending partnership
Dispute Resolution: How disagreements are handled
Signatories: Authorized representatives of each party

content.text: Partner schools use the Essential MOU Elements list above as their working MOU tool. (A separate Partnership MOU Template, T-36, is registered in Section 19.2 as not yet written. When it is published, it will replace this list.)
All partnerships are reviewed every year: Review Criteria:
content.title: 23.7.3 Partnership Review and Evaluation

items: Achievement of stated objectives

Alignment with school values and strategic priorities
Stakeholder feedback (students, parents, staff)

Partner satisfaction

content.text: Review Process:

Decision: Continue, modify, or terminate
Documentation and communication of decision

editorialNotes.title: Note on this table
editorialNotes.text: The source image labeled the first column "CIS Standard" and filed the counseling evidence under a phantom letter-C domain named for student support, with a third row ("Student Wellbeing") carrying no domain letter. Neither matched the current CIS framework (Domains A-I): student support and wellbeing evidence belongs to Domain E (Wellbeing). In the 2026-08-20 correction pass both rows were re-filed and combined under Domain E; the Domain H row was already correct. Cross-check against the CIS/WASC mapping in Section 24 before using as accreditation evidence.

editorialNotes.title: Note on this table
editorialNotes.text: The "Category E: Culture" row in the source image is wrong and has been re-filed under Category C. ACS WASC Focus on Learning, 2019 edition defines Categories A-D only - the string "Category E" does not appear anywhere in the manual - and school culture sits in Category C, Support for Student Personal and Academic Growth. The alumni-engagement and community-partnership evidence in that row is real and should be re-filed under an existing category (Category A: Organization, or Category D) when Section 24 mapping is refreshed. Categories C and A in the other two rows are valid.
